chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them both)
Regarding a man who touches his nose during prayer and sees blood, what should he do? Should he leave (the prayer)? He said: 'If it is dry, he should throw it away and there is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: Does dry blood on the nose invalidate prayer or require leaving?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib clarifies the ruling on minor impurities (najasah) encountered during Salah, establishing that dry blood does not invalidate the prayer, reflecting the Shia principle that only fresh, flowing blood is typically considered major impurity in this context. It highlights the practical ease (yusr) in ritual law, allowing the worshipper to continue their devotion without interruption, provided the dried residue is removed.
